chunks: 33 - Ahmad narrated; he said: Ali ibn al-Hasan at-Taymali narrated from his book in Rajab, the year 277 AH; he said: Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Yazeed (the seller of Sabr) and Muhammad ibn al-Walid ibn Khalid al-Khazzaz both narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) say:
A caller from the Heaven will call out by the name of the Master of this Matter, saying: 'Verily, the authority/command belongs to So-and-so son of So-and-so.' Then what is the fighting for?

key_terms.صَاحِبُ هَذَا الْأَمْرِ: The Master of this Matter (referring to the Imam/Mahdi)
key_terms.مُنَادٌ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ: A caller from the Heaven (a divine announcer)

ai.seo_question: What is the sign of the divine caller announcing the Mahdi's identity?
ai.summary: Recorded by al-Nu'mani in his seminal work *Kitab al-Ghayba*, this hadith highlights the 'Nadim al-Sama’' (Heavenly Caller) as a definitive, miraculous sign that resolves the 'Khufah' (ambiguity) of leadership during the Minor and Major Ghaiba. By explicitly naming the Imam, this divine proclamation eliminates sectarian disputes and validates the authority of the specific descendant, reinforcing the Shia doctrine of explicit designation (Nass).
